service_metadata.portal_name: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities

eligibility_criteria: Disability assessment and certification are carried out according to the disability-specific assessment guidelines issued under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.
The certifying authority is designated by the State Government or Union Territory Administration.
The disability certificate is issued by the designated certifying authority within its notified jurisdiction.
Different assessment and certification criteria apply to different categories of disabilities.
दिव्यांगता का आकलन और प्रमाणन दिव्यांग व्यक्तियों के अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 के तहत जारी संबंधित दिव्यांगता-विशिष्ट दिशानिर्देशों के अनुसार किया जाता है।
प्रमाणित करने वाले अधिकारी को राज्य सरकार या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश प्रशासन द्वारा नामित किया जाता है।

assessment_information: For multiple disabilities, each disability is assessed separately.
Only individual disabilities of 25% or more are included in the composite disability calculation.
The composite disability percentage cannot exceed 100%.
For visual impairment, assessment is performed after the best possible correction.
For autism spectrum disorder, disability assessment depends on age and severity.
For children below 6 years with autism spectrum disorder, the certificate is temporary and reassessment is required between 6 and 7 years.
For persons aged 18 years or above with autism spectrum disorder, the disability certificate issued after the age of 18 is permanent.
For intellectual disability, the minimum age for certification is one completed year.
For children below 5 years with Global Developmental Delay, a temporary certificate is issued until the age of 5 years.
For mental illness, permanent certification generally requires a minimum duration of at least two years, subject to the applicable guidelines.

fees.details: The provided assessment guidelines do not specify the citizen application fee for a disability certificate.

vector_db_chunks.text: Disability Certificate: Disability assessment and certification are carried out according to disability-specific guidelines issued under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. The State Government or Union Territory Administration designates qualified certifying authorities, who issue disability certificates within their notified jurisdiction.

The assessment guidelines cover locomotor disability, visual impairment, hearing and speech/language disability, specific learning disability, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, mental illness, blood disorders, multiple disabilities and chronic neurological conditions.

For multiple disabilities, each disability is assessed separately. Only individual disabilities of 25 percent or more are included in the composite disability calculation. The composite disability percentage cannot exceed 100 percent.

For autism spectrum disorder, children below 6 years are given a temporary certificate and require reassessment between 6 and 7 years. For children aged 6 years and above but below 18 years, reassessment and re-certification are performed according to the applicable age and disability criteria. A certificate issued at 18 years of age is valid lifelong.

For intellectual disability, the minimum age for certification is one completed year. Children above one year and up to 5 years may be diagnosed with Global Developmental Delay. Children below 5 years receive a temporary certificate valid until age 5. For children aged 5 years and above, validity and reassessment depend on the disability percentage and age.

For mental illness, the assessment may include clinical assessment, the Indian Disability Evaluation and Assessment Scale (IDEAS), and/or IQ assessment where required. Permanent certification generally requires a minimum duration of at least two years of mental illness, subject to the applicable assessment guidelines.

A reassessment application may contain the applicant's name, parents' names, date of birth, sex, permanent and current address, contact details, type and percentage of disability, existing certificate details and reason for reassessment. Listed supporting documents include the existing disability certificate, relevant medical records where applicable, proof of change of residence where applicable and two recent passport-size photographs.
